clue.text: Mark, a seaman, wanted a sacred symbol

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor called Mark is on the hunt for some holy emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is a common noun here; 'wanted' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab beetle was a holy emblem in ancient Egypt, carved as amulets and seals.

clue.text: The beasts, to strike in a recession!

indicators.note: a recession is a going back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: to slam is to strike hard
taken as written

explanation.surface: An economic slump turns people into savages who lash out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recession' sounds economic, but it is the reversal signal: SLAM IN A, read backwards, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Beasts are creatures of the non-human kind, the general word for which is this plural.

clue.text: Signalling system found heaps more adaptable

indicators.note: something adaptable can be reshaped, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a flexible method of sending messages using heaps more flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is a method of sending messages by flag or arm positions, a visual signalling code.

clue.text: Plant a guy had quite some time

parts.note: a guy had, contracted, is he'd: a man had
an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Some fellow has had a long stretch of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a guy had' becomes the contraction HE'D, minus its apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedera is the botanical genus name for ivy, a climbing evergreen.

clue.text: Much like soldiers succeeding amid chaos

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so the soldiers follow the scrambled letters
chaos is disorder, so the letters of the word amid are scrambled

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops making progress in the middle of turmoil are much liked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaos' reads like part of the scene but is the anagram signal; 'succeeding' means coming after, not achieving success.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something with warm approval or respect is to like it very much.

clue.text: There's nothing left, that's agreed

definitions.meaning: read jokily, everything is on the right-hand side, so none remains on the left
an expression of consent, like OK

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a play: if everything is on the right, nothing is left.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means OK or very well when agreeing, and jokily means every item is on the right side.

clue.text: A Scotsman gets on in France

definitions.note: a place found in France: the definition names a French town by its location

parts.note: Mac, from the common surname prefix, is a crossword Scotsman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scot is making headway while living in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link; the definition is loose, pointing to a town located in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Macon is a town on the Saône in Burgundy, famous for its wine.

clue.text: The pretty girl in red was plainly not content

indicators.note: in tells us the pretty girl sits inside the word red

parts.note: taken as written
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A beautiful girl in a red dress was obviously unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' looks like the colour of her dress but is simply the container; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise up in revolt is a clear show of discontent with authority.

clue.text: Yields at one time occupying many of the French

indicators.note: occupying means filling the inside, so the time word sits within the other letters

parts.note: C is the Roman hundred, crossword shorthand for many
des means of the in French
once means formerly

explanation.surface: The French gave way long ago when their land was occupied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' suggests a military occupation but signals one piece going inside the other; DES is French for 'of the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way in an argument or contest is to admit defeat or grant a point.

clue.text: A little holiday place bound to make a person feel better

definitions.text: to make a person feel better

indicators.note: a little of the phrase is taken, a run of letters lodged in holiday place bound

explanation.surface: A small getaway destination is certain to cheer someone up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' tells you to take part of 'place bound'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill has no active drug but can make a patient feel better through belief alone.

clue.text: The odd university man composing music to dance to

parts.note: rum is old British slang for strange
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: An eccentric graduate writes tunes for dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composing' is just a link here, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance and the rhythm played for it.

clue.text: A reasonable account for a limited supply of beer?

parts.note: a ration is a fixed, limited allowance
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone justifies why only a little beer is being handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning or justification behind a decision.

clue.text: A party causing trouble

parts.note: a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: A celebration causing a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuss or bother, as in 'much ado about nothing'.

clue.text: Perhaps he'll daub fish

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A man might smear paint about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals rearranging the letters of HELL and DAUB.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullhead is a big-headed freshwater fish, also called the miller's thumb.

clue.text: Giving direction to cast is happiness indeed!

indicators.note: giving here means adding on, so the compass point is attached to the throwing word

parts.note: to heave is to throw or cast
N, north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Telling the actors where to go turns out to be pure bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like actors but means throw; N, a compass point, is added to HEAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of perfect bliss is called heaven, the paradise of supreme happiness.

clue.text: Contemplates exercise for a personal problem

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it closely
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: Someone thinking about working out finds a private difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching vision from overuse is a problem one suffers individually.

clue.text: Chastened tot nicer maybe as a result

indicators.note: maybe suggests another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child, punished, ends up better behaved.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sorry and remorseful after being put in one's place.

clue.text: Transport without a light

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Transport without a light' (3): RAY is light, but no transport word less A gives RAY; probably a letter was lost in OCR (DRAY without D).

clue.text: A horse and sheep in need of sorting out!

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
rams are male sheep

explanation.surface: A horse and some sheep need rounding up.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: these word puzzles need their letters put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbled words are puzzles whose letters must be rearranged to solve them.

clue.text: A good man, yet initially in beastly accommodation

parts.note: ST, a saint, is a crossword good man

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word yet

explanation.surface: Even a decent fellow might end up living in squalor.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigsty is housing for pigs, so lodging for beasts.

clue.text: A note of years gone by very valuable

parts.note: G is a musical note
olden means of former times

explanation.surface: A musical note from long ago is precious indeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made of the precious yellow metal is highly prized.

clue.text: A river in a very picturesque area

indicators.note: in tells us the river is lodged within the words

explanation.surface: A river runs through a beautiful bit of countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ure is a Yorkshire river flowing through Wensleydale.

clue.text: Brown's after top players much may turn on it

indicators.note: after puts the colour word behind the players

parts.note: caps are players capped for their country
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown is following the best players in sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Caps are awarded to players selected for national sides; the definition is cryptic, a capstan being a rotating winch.
explanation.definitionFit: A capstan is a revolving drum on ships for winding cable, so much rotates about it.

clue.text: Communists cutting following will get the bird

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Communists cutting following will get the bird' (8): REDS + START fits, but 'cutting' and 'following' have no clear jobs as held; possibly garbled.
annotationWithheld.clue: Communists cutting following will get the bird

clue.text: Eastern American law-man about to charm a woman

indicators.note: about means around, so the lawyer's letters go round the charm word

parts.note: a DA is a US district attorney
to win over is to charm

explanation.surface: An American lawyer from the East sets out to win a lady's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals that the American lawyer surrounds the charm word, with the Eastern abbreviation in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Edwina is a female given name.

clue.text: An artist having the wind up?

definitions.meaning: J. M. W. ..., the English painter
jokily, someone who winds things round, a rotator

explanation.walkthrough: 'having the wind up' usually means being scared; here it means one who turns.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. W. Turner painted landscapes; literally one who rotates or winds things.

clue.text: Novel about the Left hundreds would have repressed

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the unfamiliar word wraps round the left

parts.note: novel means new and unfamiliar, strange
L is the abbreviation for left
D is the Roman numeral 500, several hundreds

explanation.surface: A book about the political Left would have been suppressed by many.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but is an adjective; 'about' puts L inside STRANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangled cry or feeling is choked back and held in.

clue.text: Like to write, but shaky

parts.note: as means like
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: Someone wanting to write is unsteady.
explanation.definitionFit: Trembling like the poplar whose leaves quiver in the lightest breeze.

clue.text: Revolting individual seen in flight

definitions.meaning: one who rises up against authority, a rebel
part of a flight of stairs, the vertical piece of a step

explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' means a staircase, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel rises up; the upright board of each step in a staircase has the same name.

clue.text: The underworld boss quietly rested only for show

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
P, piano, means quietly in music
lay is the past of lie, to rest

explanation.surface: The mob boss lay low only for appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibition or show put on for viewers.

clue.text: Suggest it-name it quite wrongly

indicators.note: quite wrongly means the letters are put wholly out of order

explanation.surface: Someone names something, completely incorrectly.
explanation.definitionFit: To intimate is to hint or imply.

clue.text: Leading Oriental coppers backed this economist

parts.note: key means main or leading

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the coin word is reversed

parts.note: the sen is a small copper coin of Japan and other Asian countries

explanation.surface: Senior Eastern police officers supported this economist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the British economist behind Keynesian theory.
